title: Dedicated capacity ops slate for threshold-driven workflows
creator: Elena Park
description:
Goal: Design a compact, action-oriented ops slate for dedicated GPU pools that surfaces health signals, autoscale intent, burst budgets, and cost impact in a single glance while enabling safe operator actions (quick scale, block burst, start canary).

Problem context: Operators need a compact control surface that fits onto the Redwood Console fleet view and on small secondary monitors in NOC. Current designs are either too verbose (full telemetry pages) or too shallow (single KPI tiles). This slate should be legible at 1200px width and modular enough to exist as an expanded drawer from the main pool list.

Key components to design:
- Health header: pool status pill (OK/WARN/CRIT), aggregated SLO adherence percent, last incident marker.
- Trend row: small sparkline for latency p95, queue depth, GPU utilization, thermal index. Sparklines include anomaly markers and tooltips with last 24h delta.
- Burst budget meter: visual remaining burst credits, projected depletion time at current burn rate, soft-limit slider for auto-throttles.
- Autoscale intent card: current policy (min/max/step), predicted scale recommendation (based on 10m lookahead), one-click apply with confirmation and audit trail.
- Cost preview: estimated $/hr delta for applying autoscale or burst for N minutes; toggles for conservative vs aggressive recommendation.
- Quick actions: pause accepting new jobs, force scale +1/ +3 nodes, enable burst override for N minutes, open canary rollout composer. Actions require role-based confirmation and list of affected customers if enabled.

Acceptance criteria:
1) High-fidelity screens for collapsed and expanded slate states.
2) Prototype in Figma with interactive sparklines and confirmation flows.
3) Usability test (5 operators) with success metric: >80% can complete "limit bursts to 20% of budget" task in under 90s.
4) Engineering handoff with component spec (tokens, spacing, states) and accessibility notes.

Design constraints & trade-offs considered:
- Density vs clarity: we favored a compact row-based layout that reveals additional metrics in an expanding panel rather than cram all metrics into a single tile.
- Action safety: any destructive or cost-impacting control requires 2-step confirmation with reason log and optional incident reference. This adds friction but reduces accidental cost overruns.
- Data latency: some metrics (thermals, queue depth) update every 15s; stateful actions reflect last known telemetry and indicate staleness.

Security & compliance: quick actions must be gated by RBAC and emit audit logs. The UI includes an inline indicator if the current user lacks permission for a visible action (button disables with tooltip).

Notes for engineers: we propose a new "ops-slate" React component composed of small atoms: StatusPill, CompactSparkline (svg), BudgetMeter, PolicyPreview, CostDeltaBadge, and ActionMenu. Each must accept a mode prop (collapsed | expanded) and support keyboard-only interactions.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Marco Silva (PM): Reviewed initial wireframes. Liked compact layout. Asked for a clearer separation between predictive recommendations and current policy. Suggested cost delta badges next to each action.

2025-02-18 - Elena Park (Designer): Updated prototype to add CostDeltaBadge and moved confirmation flow into a slide-over. Uploaded Figma link in attachments. Noted two outstanding questions: (1) show thermal index numeric vs color; (2) whether burst override should be a timed toggle or a one-off credit spend.

2025-02-21 - Priya Nair (SRE): Spike feedback - prefer timed toggles for auditability. Also requested an explicit estimated impact on SLA percentage when forcing scale-down. Marked as dependency for ENG-4219 (autoscaler API).

2025-02-27 - Marcus Chen (Design Lead): High-fidelity screens ready. Ran quick accessibility audit: color contrast OK for status pills but budget meter needs an alternate text pattern for colorblind modes. Added notes to component spec.

2025-03-03 - Anna Gomez (Engineering): Feasibility review: CompactSparkline will reuse existing telemetry endpoint but requires a small aggregation endpoint; created ENG-4361 to add 1m rolling aggregates. Action gating will tie into RBAC v2 (ENG-3890).

2025-03-04 - UX Research (Kofi Mensah): Scheduled moderated usability sessions for 2025-03-07; test script in attachments. Focus: comprehension of budget meter and speed of applying safe autoscale recommendation.
